title: Everyday Writing Assistant
problem: New users often ask AI to 'write an email about X' and get a generic, off-tone draft they end up heavily rewriting — because the model wasn't given the two things that actually determine good writing: who it's going to, and what you want to happen after they read it.

workflow.detail: Name the recipient and your relationship to them — a message to your manager and one to a close coworker should sound different, and the model needs to know which.
Not just the topic — what should happen after they read it? Reply by Friday? Agree to a meeting? Feel reassured? This shapes tone and structure more than the topic does.

workflow.step: 3. Give key points as bullet notes
workflow.detail: Jot rough bullet points, not full sentences — let the model handle the prose. Full sentences tend to get copied verbatim and read stiffly.
Run the Prompt Template with a tone description (e.g. 'direct but warm, no corporate jargon') and a rough length.

workflow.step: 5. Read it out loud before sending
workflow.detail: The fastest way to catch a tone mismatch. If a phrase doesn't sound like something you'd actually say, edit it — a draft is a draft, not your final voice.

variables.name: RELATIONSHIP
variables.label: Your relationship to them
variables.placeholder: e.g. Professional but not close; we've emailed a handful of times

variables.name: DESIRED_OUTCOME
variables.label: Desired outcome
variables.placeholder: e.g. Get the broken heater fixed this week, in writing so there's a record

variables.name: KEY_POINTS
variables.label: Key points (bullet notes)
variables.placeholder:
- Heater stopped working Tuesday
- Apartment is 58°F
- Already tried resetting the breaker
- Need it fixed by Friday

variables.name: TONE
variables.label: Tone
variables.placeholder: e.g. Polite but firm, no exclamation points

exampleOutput:
Subject: Heater Repair Needed This Week

Hi [Landlord],

Our heater stopped working on Tuesday and the apartment has been at 58°F since. I reset the breaker, which didn't resolve it. Could someone come take a look and repair it by Friday? Please let me know a time that works.

Thanks,
[Name]
tips: Bullet notes, not full sentences, in KEY_POINTS — full sentences tend to get copied verbatim and read stiffly next to the model's own prose.
Always read the draft out loud before sending — it's the fastest way to catch a tone mismatch.
Save a TONE description that works for you (e.g. 'direct but warm, no corporate jargon') and reuse it across prompts for a consistent voice over time.
For anything sensitive or high-stakes (HR, legal, a difficult personal message), use the draft as a starting point you heavily edit — not something to send unread.
